Makah

Makah Tribe publications offer a starting path through coastal village life, maritime knowledge and the Makah Cultural and Research Center. The historical account and museum introduction connect living community interpretation with material recovered at Ozette; fuller archaeology and individual objects require separate review.

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Identity and homelands

Makah homelands lie around Cape Flattery and Neah Bay, with a strong relationship to the sea and its resources.

Read the sources [1] Makah Tribe

02

Historical context

The Tribe’s history links oral tradition and archaeological evidence, including the Ozette village site, with continuing community life.

Read the sources [1] Makah Tribe

03

Living communities and further study

The International Whaling Commission’s account details the cultural and nutritional importance of whaling and the Treaty of Neah Bay’s reserved rights.

Read the sources [2] International Whaling Commission

04

Coastal villages and different kinds of canoes

The Tribe’s historical account describes permanent shore villages and seasonal movements connected with fishing and gathering. It explains that cedar canoes served different purposes, including transport and several kinds of marine harvesting. This community-authored description connects maritime skill with everyday and extended-family life without reducing Makah history to one activity.

Read the sources [1] Makah Tribe

05

A museum interpreted by the community

The Tribe presents the Makah Cultural and Research Center as a place to learn from material recovered at the Ozette village site. Its account distinguishes archaeological belongings from historic material and replicas used in interpretation. This is a useful introduction to community-led presentation; the excavation record and each displayed object need their own reading and reuse checks.

Read the sources [3] Makah Tribe

Makah Tribe history — coastal villages and maritime life ↗

The Tribe describes coastal villages, seasonal movement and the practical diversity of canoes. Begin with its account of relationships between sea, land and family life.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete public historical body under Makah Tribe history, Makah Tribe Villages, and Ecological Practices & Mariner Skills; web lines 37–47. Navigation, photographs and later linked subjects are not source readings.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Actual HTML body read normally. No underlying archaeological reports, oral-history recordings, maps, present boundary or contemporary population figures checked. This is the Tribe’s own historical synthesis; no universal clothing, ceremony or art-reproduction permission inferred.

https://makah.com/makah-tribal-info/about-history/

Makah Museum at the Makah Cultural and Research Center ↗

The Tribe explains how its museum interprets material recovered at Ozette, including the difference between recovered belongings, historic material and replicas. Individual collection objects need their own study and permissions.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete substantive museum-introduction and Visiting the Museum paragraphs, web lines 37–42, plus the historical opening-year statement at 46. Admission and operating information were not adopted.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Actual public HTML prose read; no gallery images copied, linked Ozette site publication read, original excavation report checked, or present hours verified. The interpretation is the Tribe’s visitor-facing museum account. The stated archaeological dating is attributed, not independently redated.
